verification_notes: Route count in era (open at 2002-12-31, per fetched sources): C1, C2 (partial), B, 1-Haneda, 1-Ueno, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6-Mukojima, 6-Misato, 7, 9, 11, Y, K1, K3, K5, K6 (partial, 2002-04-30 section), S1, S5 (1998 section), S2 (entrance only, 2000). K2 has no verified section data.
Routes not open at reference: 10 (Harumi, 2009/2018), K7 (Yokohama North, 2017/2020), S2 main sections (2004/2006), C2 western half (2007/2010/2015, incl. Yamate Tunnel, excluded).
There is no route 8 in the list. S2 says the 8 route designation is vacant and that the 1966-07-02 Kyobashi JCT was built when route 8 was completed. Treated as not a separate route.

Route list: the Japanese wiki overview S2 names routes C1, C2, B, Y, 1 Ueno, 1 Haneda, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 Mukojima, 6 Misato, 7, 9, 10, 11, K1, K2, K3, K5, K6, K7, S1, S2, S5. The English wiki S1 page gave a similar list; route-level detail was not in the English article.

Official shutoko.jp route page (S22) returned HTTP 429 twice. The official navi-map (S23) was not fetched. Official opening-date data therefore comes only from Wikipedia-derived fetches and must be checked against shutoko.jp before use.

Two per-route Japanese Wikipedia pages (S20 Omiya, S21 Kawasaki) returned HTTP 404 for the titles used; S5 Omiya data comes only from the S2 overview and S6/K6 data comes only from the S2 overview. The S19 Kawaguchi page was fetched successfully.

Fetched text was summarized by a small model and contains internal inconsistencies. Specific conflicts: 1-Haneda length by section (S2 vs S5); 5-Ikebukuro 1977 section (10.5 km S10 vs 8.6 km S2) and 1990 section (0.8 km S10 vs 2.6 km S2); 9-Fukagawa total length (5.3 km S14 vs 7.0 km S2); 6-Mukojima 1971 section (7.9 km S2 vs 6.24 planned S11); K1/K2 assignment of the 1978 Kinko-Yokohama Koen section (S17 vs S2); K5 1989 section (4.6 km S18 vs 8.8 km S2); S1 start point (Senju-shinbashi 16.5 km S2 vs Kohoku JCT 12.3 km S19); C2 Yotsugi section (1.4 km S2 vs 0.9 km S4) and 2002 Itabashi-Kohoku section (7.1 km S2 vs 6.5 km S4).

Opening dates were cross-checked where two or more sources agreed (for example 1-Haneda 1963/1964/1966, 2 1967-09-30, 3 1971-12-21, 4 1976-05-18, 5 1993-10-26, 6-Mukojima 1971/1982, 7 1971-03-21, 9 1980-02-05, 11 1993-08-26, B 1976-2001, K1 1968-1984, K5 1989-09-27, C2 2002-12-25, 6-Misato 1985-01-24). Single-source dates are flagged in segment notes.
name_en values are transliterations generated for this manifest. The sources did not supply official English names for junctions or interchanges. Treat them as placeholders, not official names.
length_km values are null where no source stated them. Lengths marked as derived were computed from km markers in S3/S4/S5 tables and are approximate.

length_km_total_current is null for most routes. Only infobox values fetched from per-route pages were entered (1-Haneda 13.8, 1-Ueno 4.4, 2 5.9, 3 11.7, 4 13.5, 5 21.5, 6-Mukojima 6.24, 6-Misato 10.6, 7 10.4, 9 5.3, 11 5.0, K1 19.7, K5 4.6, S1 12.3). Network total 337.8 km (2025) is from S2; not per route and not era-specific.
Status enum: 'closed_later' is used for sections open at reference that were closed afterward (Y-2). Sections opened after 2002-12-31 use 'not_yet_open'.
Yamate Tunnel: part of C2 Oi-Ohashi section, opened 2015-03-07 (S4). Excluded as not in era.
Several interchange and junction opening years are not stated in any fetched source. These are left null or 'year not stated' in notes rather than inferred.
Not verified: directional restrictions (directions field) were taken from source wording where given; otherwise 'both' is a default assumption, not a source fact.

Not verified: operator names for external connections (Tomei, Chuo, Higashi-Kanto, Joban, Tokyo Gaikan, Keiyo, Yokohama-Yokosuka) are from general knowledge and labelled as such in notes where relevant.
